subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should lease-bound external-orchestrator session spawning become a permanent OpenClaw core Gateway and shared-state contract, or should the owner-specific lifecycle remain in an external plugin/adapter behind a generic core seam?
rationale: The patch is not a narrow repair: it introduces a named external integration contract, new Gateway methods, durable state, discovery metadata, and compatibility obligations. Repository policy assigns optional owner-specific workflows outside core when existing seams can support them, so implementation quality alone cannot settle ownership.

options.title: Use an external owner boundary
options.body: Keep the orchestrator-specific lease, metadata, and replay lifecycle in an external plugin or adapter and add only the smallest generic core seam that is demonstrably missing.

options.title: Sponsor a core Gateway contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the seven methods, persistence model, documentation, compatibility guarantees, and long-term ownership as permanent core API.

recommendation.title: Use an external owner boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the orchestrator-specific lease, metadata, and replay lifecycle in an external plugin or adapter and add only the smallest generic core seam that is demonstrably missing.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate for the core-versus-external ownership decision across Gateway, session spawning, and shared state.
